reviews.title: Excellent Cooling, Beautiful Lighting, Zero Hassle
reviews.comment:
This water cooling setup has exceeded all my expectations. It works flawlessly—keeps my CPU running at the perfect temperature even under heavy load, and it’s whisper quiet while doing it. Installation was straightforward, and the build quality feels solid and reliable.
One of the standout features is the LED customization. The fan lighting patterns are fully customizable, and the software makes it super easy to set everything up just the way you want. Best of all, the configuration actually saves and loads correctly—even across different operating systems—which is a rare and very welcome surprise.
No complaints at all so far. If you’re looking for a high-quality water cooling solution with awesome lighting and zero hassle, this one’s a great choice.  Great value for the money.
reviews.author: Jay

reviews.title: Excellent Cooling Performance with Stunning ARGB Effects
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1ACEVbAspL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/71xy0ZHbO-L._SY256.jpg I recently installed the ID-COOLING FX360 INF 360mm AIO liquid cooler in my new build, and it’s been a fantastic upgrade. First off, the cooling performance is top-notch — it keeps my Ryzen/Intel CPU running cool even under heavy load, with temperatures staying impressively low. The included 3x120mm fans are quiet, even at high speeds, with a max noise level of just 27.2dB(A), which is great for a near-silent setup.
What really sets this cooler apart is the ARGB infinity mirror on the pump — it looks absolutely stunning in a tempered glass case. The lighting is vibrant, smooth, and syncs easily with my motherboard’s ARGB header. The daisy-chained fans also simplify cable management, making the installation much cleaner and easier.
Mounting was straightforward, with clear instructions and wide compatibility across both Intel (LGA1851/1700/1200/115X) and AMD (AM5/AM4) sockets. The build quality feels solid throughout.
Overall, this cooler combines performance, aesthetics, and ease of installation in one great package. Highly recommended for gamers and PC builders who want both form and function.
reviews.author: Le1

reviews.title: ID-Cooling FX360 INF - Great Price & Performance!
reviews.comment:
I built a computer for an arcade I was building and didn’t know what I needed to run the emulators. So I used an i9 14900k with an Asus ROG Strix 4090 OC because no one would tell me what would work. So, I used the motto go big or go home. Needless to say it was overkill and then I find out that the i9 runs hot and my DeepCool AK620 worked for the emulator games, but not for AAA Steam games. My CPU kept thermal throttling.
I purchased an Artic Liquid Freezer III 420, but was unable to get it to fit into my Lian Li Lancool III case. So I purchased this ID-Cooling FX360 INF since it got great reviews from those who do PC content.
I’ve had this now for about 2 months and I’ve never had an issue with thermal throttling since. The highest temps I’ve seen is 70C-75C and that was during a CPU-Z stress test. Idling I’m around 30C-32C and playing 2 AAA games (Indian Jones & Hogwarts), at 4k, the highest I’ve seen is around 60C.
This AIO has worked flawlessly and like a lot of people have said, it was really easy to install.
Because it’s inside my arcade pedestal (and fears of my CPU over heating) mines set to run at 100% all the time and the fan noise isn’t bad at all. Those that complain the fans are loud or the pump is loud, I wish they were around in the 80’s and 90’s when fans were extremely loud!! They’d think twice about calling these loud. Only time will tell as to how well it holds up.
reviews.author: T.J.

reviews.title: Surprisingly good cooling performance for its cheap price, if you can tolerate cheap build quality.
reviews.comment:
This is a very performant AIO for its price. Even included with a sizable (I made two applications) thermal paste that also has good reviews.
However, the included fans wobble and create vibration noise when ramping up. They would physically shake your whole case. A full replacement with better fans is recommended.
The pump produces a high-frequency resonance whine after 64% and slowly creeps louder and louder to 100%. I have to cap my pump to 63% in software. The pump whine isn't too loud compared to the fan, but the high frequency makes it unbearable to me.
Also, be aware that the pump is connected with a 3-pin DC header, not the advertised 4-pin PWM. Make sure your motherboard can do and is configured to voltage control on pump headers; otherwise, your pump will be stuck with 100% RPM.
Aside from build quality, the raw cooling performance of this AIO is very good. It's the best you can get in this price range.
reviews.author: Kaltu

reviews.title: Great cooler, great price
reviews.comment:
I grabbed the ID-COOLING FX360 INF as a replacement when my NZXT Kraken cooler failed and my CPU temps were hitting the 90°C range. At just $70 compared to $250 for a new Kraken, I figured it was worth a shot — and I’m glad I did. Installation was quick and easy, and it even fit right into the same mounting setup I had from the Kraken, which made the swap hassle-free.
Now my CPU is idling around 34°C, and the cooler runs quietly with a nice ARGB infinity mirror effect that looks great in the case. For the price, this cooler seriously overdelivers and I’m very happy with the performance so far.
reviews.author: Stephen Gubele
